label: Vigilance & acting over time
blurb: How do planning agents manage to act over time? Through vigilance, the self-regulatory capacity that manages attention, memory, and control over scattered actions.

label: Negligence & responsibility
blurb: When and why are we blameworthy for unwitting omissions and forgetting, and what theory of responsible agency — capacity, value, or self-trust — best explains it?

label: Self-trust
blurb: Trust in one’s own future and past self as a precondition of planning agency — and what its erosion means for responsibility, psychiatry, and neurotechnology.

label: Free will & the folk
blurb: What ordinary people believe about free will and determinism — and whether the experiments that purport to measure those beliefs actually do.

label: Mind-wandering & thought
blurb: What mind-wandering is, whether it can be intentional, and how the dynamics of unguided thought fit a theory of agency.

label: Self-control & cognitive control
blurb: Self-control reconceived as coordination rather than willpower, grounded in the computational structure of cognitive control — in humans and machines.

label: Moral cognition & its paradigms
blurb: The psychology of moral judgment — cooperation, purity, character — and a critique of whether trolley-style paradigms capture moral cognition at all.

label: Carving the mind
blurb: Metaphysics and methodology of the cognitive sciences: cognitive ontology, mental imagery, memory, and the question of which kinds cognitive science should be built around.

label: Trust in science & public reason
blurb: What norms govern the use of scientific information in public deliberation, and how should science position itself in public life to foster public trust in the institution?

label: Disagreement & democracy
blurb: The epistemology of political disagreement: why warmth doesn’t fix democracy, what partisans get wrong about each other, and when discounting an opponent’s reasons is rational.

label: History of philosophy
blurb: Miscellaneous work on figures in the history of philosophy, mainly focused on historical theories of agency, free will, and causation.

label: Other
blurb: Standalone work in metaethics, philosophy of language, and adjacent areas.
